title: lbm: wall laws for the Spalart–Allmaras model, and a half-way on-node wall, on the CPU and the GPU
body:
Han's on-node wall takes Spalding's law, which is low in the buffer layer; with the SA model a first node at y⁺ 5 to 15 reads a channel 3 to 5 % off.

Proposal, in six stacked PRs: the SA model's own constant-stress law (CPU); a half-way variant of the on-node wall that keeps obstacle size and reads the law at the second open cell (CPU); the on-node wall at obstacles, edges and corners on the GPU; SA with Han's wall on the GPU; the SA law on the GPU; the half-way wall on the GPU.

Related, not touched: #927 and #938 (wall models on interpolated walls and wall-modelled LES channels).

title: lbm: wall function for the Spalart–Allmaras model, and Han's on-node wall at obstacles, edges and inlets
body:
With a wall model, the SA model (#1007, issue #1006) has no wall treatment of its own at the first fluid node.

Proposal, in five stacked pull requests: (a) the Nichols & Nelson wall function: ν̃ at each first fluid node from the eddy viscosity of the law the wall applies; (b) Han, Ooka & Kikumoto's on-node wall (eq. 14) on obstacle walls, by link pairs; (c) where it meets an inlet, outlet or slip face; (d) the SA wall distance reading the halfway links beside the nodes; (e) an inlet cell touching two walls becomes a wall cell.

All opt-in with `spalding_bounce`/`musker`; CPU first, the GPU refuses what it does not run.

Overlaps #927 and #938 (wall models); we would like to know what should wait for them.

title: Interpolated walls make or lose mass: the mean density drifts on walls that cut the grid
body:
On a wall that does not lie half way along its links, the interpolated rule returns another amount than left along the link. A turned 8-cell laminar channel (periodic, body force, no model) drifts in mean density by up to 2.7e-2 per 10,000 steps with the linear rule and 2e-2 with the quadratic one (24 cases in the turned-channel test).

Proposal: store what each wall node's links create at a step and take it back from the node and its fluid neighbours one step later, weights renormalised over the fluid targets, no momentum added; off by default, CPU and GPU, open boundaries untouched.

Question: should it be a `solve.fluid` option, and under what name?

title: Linux/GNOME Wayland: window closes while orbiting a heavy fluid result (`Connection reset by peer`, `WinitEventLoop(ExitFailure(1))`); fine under XWayland
body:
### Observed failure

Orbiting the viewport with the mouse over a large fluid result closes the FieldCraft window. No crash report is written (`fieldcraft-cli crashes list` shows nothing new), and the log ends with:

```
Io error: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)
Io error: Connection reset by peer (os error 104)
Error: WinitEventLoop(ExitFailure(1))
```

The same model under XWayland (`env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY WINIT_UNIX_BACKEND=x11 fieldcraft`) can be orbited without problems.

### Reproduction

1. Start `fieldcraft` natively on a GNOME Wayland session.
2. Import a large closed surface as an obstacle (`geometry.import.mesh`, ~2.2 M triangles, untagged 3MF).
3. Create an air fluid domain around it with ~14 M cells (spacing 10 mm in a 3.74 × 2.3 × 1.65 m box), a velocity inlet, a convective pressure outlet and slip side walls; fluid step 7500 steps, 6 frames, `regularized` + Smagorinsky; `solve.fluid` with `backend: "gpu"`.
4. Show the velocity on the default slice with streamlines (64 seeds, 60 traced).
5. Orbit the view with the mouse for a few seconds → the window disappears.

The model is a 2.4 GB `.fieldcraft` of a private design, so I can't attach it. I haven't reduced it to a bundled sample or tested smaller scenes.

### Evidence

- App log (`/tmp/fieldcraft-automation/logs/fieldcraft.log`): the session ends with `fieldcraft: FieldCraft closed` and no warning; stderr has the three lines above.
- No crash report is created for these exits.
- Seen on native Wayland while orbiting. Under XWayland the same model and interaction work.

### Expected behaviour

Orbiting should stay responsive or at least degrade (dropped frames) without the compositor disconnecting the client.

### Investigation

Not looked at the code. My guess: frames get slow with this scene (2.2 M-triangle obstacle + 14 M-cell slice + streamlines) while pointer motion events keep arriving, and GNOME Mutter disconnects a Wayland client whose connection backs up. X11 tolerates that. Coalescing pointer motion to one update per frame, or a lighter render path while the camera moves, might avoid it. Possibly related in spirit to #683 (UI thread blocking on Wayland), but that one was file dialogs.

### Version and platform

FieldCraft 0.8.1 (c1bec5b74f), Linux tar.gz build, Ubuntu 24.04, GNOME on Wayland (Mutter), kernel 7.0.0-43, AMD Radeon RX 6650 XT, Mesa 25.2.8 RADV (Vulkan), MSAA 4x.

title: ui: Japanese text is drawn as empty boxes (file names, the browser's root, messages)
body: ### Observed failure Japanese characters are drawn as empty boxes everywhere in the window. A model saved as `片持ち梁の解析.fieldcraft` shows boxes in its tab, at the root of the browser and in the "Saved ….fieldcraft" message. The same must happen to a design or a folder with a Japanese name, and to the bodies of a design made in SolidCraft's Japanese interface. I have checked only the file name. ### Reproduction 1. `fieldcraft --sample cantilever` 2. File > Save As, name `片持ち梁の解析.fieldcraft`. 3. Look at the tab, the browser's root and the message at the bottom right. Or through MCP: `save {"path": ".../片持ち梁の解析.fieldcraft"}`, then `screenshot {"source": "window"}`. ### Evidence The machine has Japanese fonts installed (`fc-match sans:lang=ja` gives Noto Sans CJK JP), so this is not a missing system font. ### Expected behaviour Japanese text is readable wherever a name or a path is shown, as it is in SolidCraft. SolidCraft's `docs/localization.md` describes how it does this, and FieldCraft could follow it: - **Desktop:** no font is shipped. The operating system's fonts are searched (Meiryo, Yu Gothic and BIZ UDGothic on Windows, Hiragino on macOS, Noto Sans CJK on Linux) and added as fallbacks behind the interface faces. - **Web:** BIZ UDPGothic (SIL OFL 1.1, 4.7 MB) is served with the app and fetched the first time Japanese text is drawn, so a session that shows none downloads nothing. The same route serves Korean and Chinese (SolidCraft has subset faces for them), and it is what a Japanese or Korean catalogue under #801 needs first. ### Investigation - `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` installs the fonts with `solidcraft_look::fonts::install`: IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Mono and egui's own fallback faces. None has Japanese glyphs. - Nothing in `crates/ui-egui` or the apps reads a system font. - SolidCraft's search for system fonts is in its `crates/ui-egui/src/fonts.rs`, a crate FieldCraft may not depend on. `solidcraft_look::fonts` leaves the way open: its docs say a host that adds faces of its own builds on `definitions` and installs the result with `apply`. So the search would be FieldCraft's own code in `crates/ui-egui`, or adapted from SolidCraft's (MIT OR Apache-2.0, a row in ATTRIBUTION.md). - #988 adds a Hebrew fallback in `theme.rs` (system candidates, and a face embedded at build time from `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR`). A Japanese face is too large to embed in the wasm build that way, hence the fetch on demand above. - Not a cause: definition names (materials, sets, steps) are ASCII by rule (`crates/model/src/lib.rs`), so they never hold Japanese. That rule is not what this issue is about. I will open a pull request for the desktop part, following SolidCraft's way. It touches the same lines of `theme.rs` as #988, so tell me if you would rather it wait for that one. ### Version and platform FieldCraft 0.8.1 (`c1bec5b7`), desktop, Ubuntu 26.04, x86-64. Window captured offscreen through MCP `screenshot`.

title: Geometry: the space inside a hollow part as a body (waveguide interiors, internal flow)
body:
### Current behaviour

A model is built on the bodies of the open design, and sets, boundary conditions and loads name their faces (`{"body", "face"}`). The geometry commands partition, split, merge, stitch and defeature those bodies. None of them makes a body of the space a hollow part encloses.

For RFC 0001 (#971, #977) this means a waveguide drawn as its metal walls cannot be analysed as it is. The field lives in the air inside, and a port sits on the open cross-section at an end of the guide. That cross-section is an opening, not a face of any body, so there is nothing to select and nothing to mesh.

Today the way round it is to draw the interior itself in SolidCraft (for a rectangular guide, the a × b section extruded) and open that instead. That is what the RFC's verification cases do, and it is enough for them. It does not help someone who starts from the part they already have.

### What you need and why

Electromagnetic analysis meshes the space, not the part: the inside of a cavity or guide, and the conductors are its PEC boundary. Most users will arrive with the metal part. The step from that part to the space is the first thing they need, before any port or solve.

The same step serves internal flow on a body-fitted mesh, so it is not specific to RFC 0001.

### Expected behaviour

A command (say `geometry.interior`) that takes a body and its openings and adds the enclosed space as a new body:

1. The openings are named as closed loops of the body's edges (picked in the viewport as edges or as the rim of an opening).
2. Each opening is closed by a face on its loop. The kernel's `fill` already fills a closed loop of a body's edges with one face, planar when the edges lie in a plane.
3. The space bounded by those caps and the body's inner faces becomes a body of the design.

What matters for what follows:

- **The faces keep their origin.** A face of the new body that came from the part's inner wall, and a face that is a cap, can be told apart by name. Then the walls can go into one set (PEC) and each cap is a candidate port face, so picking an opening and placing a port are one action for the user.
- **A non-planar opening is refused** with a message naming it, at least at first: a waveguide port needs a flat cross-section.
- **Nothing is made when the openings do not close the space** (a loop missed): the reply says which gap is open.
- The command is part of the design's preparation like a partition: listed, deletable, replayed from the journal.

A second form, for later: the space *around* a part inside a box or sphere (the part subtracted from it), which open problems (RFC 0001 phase 4) need.

I have not checked how face names come through a boolean in `crates/geometry`; the kernel records a boolean's history (`boolean_record.rs`), so I expect it is possible.

### Who does it

This is `crates/geometry` and the kernel, outside phases 2–4. I am filing it now because it decides what the port command (`model.port.create`, phase 3) can point at. Phases 2–3 do not wait for it: their cases use interiors drawn directly. I can work on it if that is useful, or leave it to whoever owns the geometry crate.

### References

- RFC 0001 (`docs/rfc/0001-electromagnetics.md`; #971, #977), §3.4 (ports) and §3.6 (commands): no command there creates the analysis space.

title: Design iteration: study.update and study.sweep on SolidCraft parameters, the first slice of M22
body:
A user asked for a way to iterate designs. Today `geometry.open` with `model: "keep"` reopens an edited design and keeps the mesh settings and every definition (sets follow persistent face names), so a manual loop works: edit in SolidCraft, reopen, mesh, solve. Nothing automates it.

### Proposal: the first slice of M22
- `study.parameter.list`: the design's SolidCraft parameters.
- `study.update {parameters: {name: value}}`: set them, rebuild the design, reopen with `keep`, remesh with the saved settings, solve every step; one undo step; refuses with the stale references `geometry.open` reports.
- `study.sweep {parameter, values, outputs}`: run `study.update` per value and tabulate chosen outputs (max von Mises in a set, a probe, a reaction, a frequency, mass), CSV export and an XY plot.
- Deterministic and bounded (a cap on the number of runs), each run a job with progress and cancel.

Verified on a case with a closed form across the sweep (a cantilever's tip deflection against its length cubed).

Roadmap: M22.

title: Material library: more cited entries, polymers and cast irons, and a library-first material dialog (M17)
body:
A user asked for a material library. One exists (`model.material.library.list`/`.add`, nine cited structural metals: S235, S355, 304, 316, 6061-T6, 6082-T6, 7075-T6, 2024-T3, Ti-6Al-4V), but it is small and hard to find.

### Proposal
- More cited entries, each with its standard, edition and table: more structural and engineering steels (EN 10083 quenched and tempered, EN 10025 S275/S460), grey and ductile cast iron (EN 1561, EN 1563), copper alloys, more aluminium (5083, 6063), common engineering polymers (PA6, PA66-GF30, POM, PC, ABS; with the test standard and conditioning).
- Temperature-dependent values where the source gives them.
- The material dialog opens on the library browser (search, family filter), with "custom" one click away.

Roadmap: M17 (material library).

title: Contact in a linear study: the refusal and the UI offer the nonlinear step in one click (M7)
body:
A user asked for contact in linear static analysis of assemblies. Today ties (bonded) work in linear steps, and frictional contact runs in nonlinear static and explicit steps; a linear step refuses contact by name.

### Proposal
- The refusal says what to do: "contact needs a nonlinear static step: change step X's procedure (one increment is enough for small sliding)".
- In the UI, the contact dialog and `model.check` offer that change in one click (`model.step.edit` to `nonlinear_static`, small sliding, one increment), so a linear assembly study with contact is one decision away.
- The manual's contact page gets a short "contact in a linear study" section.

No change to the solvers. Roadmap: M7.

title: Loads: bearing, hydrostatic, remote force and spatially varying pressure (M7)
body:
A user doing linear static work asked for more load types. Today: force and moment (on a set or reference point), traction, pressure, gravity, body force, centrifugal, temperature (thermal strain), and mapped initial temperature or residual stress.

### Missing
- **Bearing load** on a cylindrical face: a total force distributed over the loaded half with a cosine (or parabolic) pressure, normal to the face.
- **Hydrostatic pressure**: p = ρ g (h − z) on wetted faces from a free-surface height, zero above it.
- **Remote force and moment**: a reference point at a picked location plus a distributing coupling to the faces, made in one step.
- **Pressure varying in space**: a linear or tabulated field over the faces.

Each written to all three decks, verified against a closed form (the resultant and its line of action; a hydrostatically loaded wall against beam theory).

Bolt pretension stays in M7 (`interaction.bolt`). Roadmap: M7.

title: Supports for linear static: frictionless, cylindrical, local-frame and remote displacement (M7)
body:
A user doing linear static work asked for more boundary condition types. Today: fixed, displacement (global axes), symmetry (a plane, inclined allowed), springs to ground, and a reference point with kinematic or distributing coupling.

### Missing, as one command each over what exists
- **Frictionless support** on any face, curved included: zero displacement along the face normal at each node (constraint rows `n·u = 0`, the normal averaged per node from the face's geometry).
- **Cylindrical support** on a cylindrical face: radial, axial and tangential each fixed or free, in the cylinder's own frame (from the face's axis).
- **Displacement in a local frame**: `values` in a rectangular or cylindrical coordinate system, which the two above build on.
- **Remote displacement**: a reference point plus a coupling to the picked faces, made in one step.

Each is written to all three decks as the constraints it is made of, verified against a closed form (a pressurised thick cylinder held by a cylindrical support against Lamé, a block on a frictionless curved seat against the patch-test state).

Roadmap: M7 (supports and loads for assembly investigations).

title: geometry.bodies refuses a body with keys 1 µm above a chamfer: "tessellation: face 0 (cone): edge 1: more than 20000 nodes"
body:
### Observed failure

`geometry.bodies` (and with it `inspect_model`) fails on a design whose only oddity is a 1 µm step beside a cone face:

```
the geometry operation failed: the operation failed: mesh: face 0: the operation failed: not supported yet: tessellation: face 0 (cone): tessellation: edge 1: more than 20000 nodes
```

`geometry.open` on the same file succeeds, so the design looks loaded until something asks for its faces. I met it on a wheel hub of mine (a revolved body with a chamfer and twelve dovetail keys); the reduced case below is made from primitives.

The cost climbs steeply before it fails. The same body with the step changed:

| Gap between the keys and the chamfer | `geometry.bodies` |
|---|---|
| 0 (flush) | 0.2 s |
| 0.01 mm | 6.4 s |
| 0.001 mm | refused after 19 s |

### Reproduction

A chamfered disc (a cone from r 52 to r 50 over 2 mm, then a cylinder r 50), and twelve trapezoid keys joined onto it that start 0.001 mm above the chamfer's top edge. As a SolidCraft command script (`solidcraft-cli run hub_keys.json --save hub_keys.solidcraft`, SolidCraft 0.30.1):

```json
{"commands": [
 {"command": "solid.cone", "params": {"radius": 52, "top_radius": 50, "height": 2, "name": "Chamfer"}},
 {"command": "solid.cylinder", "params": {"radius": 50, "height": 20, "base": [0, 0, 2], "operation": "join", "name": "Hub"}},
 {"command": "timeline.add", "params": {"feature": {"type": "sketch", "id": 50, "name": "Key sketch", "suppressed": false,
   "plane": {"base": {"name": "XY", "type": "origin"}, "distance": "2.001", "type": "offset"},
   "sketch": {"constraints": [], "counters": {"k": 0, "l": 4},
    "curves": [{"a": 1, "b": 2, "construction": false, "id": "l1", "type": "line"}, {"a": 2, "b": 3, "construction": false, "id": "l2", "type": "line"},
               {"a": 3, "b": 4, "construction": false, "id": "l3", "type": "line"}, {"a": 4, "b": 1, "construction": false, "id": "l4", "type": "line"}],
    "points": [{"fixed": true, "id": "origin", "pos": [0.0, 0.0]}, {"fixed": false, "id": "l1.start", "pos": [-2.0, 49.5]}, {"fixed": false, "id": "l1.end", "pos": [2.0, 48.0]},
               {"fixed": false, "id": "l2.end", "pos": [3.5, 53.0]}, {"fixed": false, "id": "l3.end", "pos": [-3.5, 53.0]}]}}}},
 {"command": "timeline.add", "params": {"feature": {"type": "extrude", "id": 51, "name": "Key", "suppressed": false, "sketch": 50, "operation": "join",
   "profiles": {"type": "all"}, "extent": {"convention": "total_distance", "direction": "positive", "distance": "15"}}}},
 {"command": "solid.pattern.circular", "params": {"features": ["Key"], "axis": "Z", "count": 12, "angle": 360}}
]}
```

Then, through `fieldcraft-cli mcp`: `execute geometry.open {"path": ".../hub_keys.solidcraft"}` (succeeds), `execute geometry.bodies {}` (the error above). With `"distance": "2.01"` in the sketch's plane it answers in 6.4 s, and with `"2"` in 0.2 s.

### Evidence

- The body is sound: one closed body of 64 faces in SolidCraft.
- SolidCraft 0.44.1 meshes all three variants at its finest export quality (`run --in hub_keys.solidcraft --out hub.stl --quality finest`), so a later SolidCraft than the pin, or its settings, copes with the step.
- On a similar disc (r 67 to r 65), a box-shaped key with the same 0.001 mm gap doesn't reach the refusal but shows the same growth: one key 4.4 s, twelve keys 41 s, against 0.1 s flush.

### Expected behaviour

The faces are listed. A 1 µm step is poor modelling, but the body is valid, and a sliver that small shouldn't refine an edge of the neighbouring cone past 20,000 nodes. If it can't be meshed, the error could name the body and say what is small, so the modelling mistake can be found: in a 52-body design it took a bisection to find which body "face 0" belonged to.

### Investigation

None in the code. From the outside: the failing face is the chamfer's cone, which the keys don't touch; they only leave a 1 µm strip of the cylinder between themselves and the cone's top edge.

### Version and platform

FieldCraft develop build of 2026-11-16 (v0.8.0), `fieldcraft-cli mcp`, Windows 11 x86_64. The design was saved by SolidCraft 0.30.1 (format 48).

title: Open a design saved by a newer SolidCraft with a notice when everything in it was read, as SolidCraft does since 0.40.0
body:
### Current behaviour

FieldCraft refuses a design whose format number is above its pin's, before reading it:

`this design was saved by a newer SolidCraft (format 58); this FieldCraft reads up to 55. Update FieldCraft to open it`

That's develop today (`Error::NewerDesign` in `crates/geometry/src/design.rs`). SolidCraft 0.42.0 (14 November) wrote format 56 and the current release, 0.44.1, writes 58, so develop opens nothing saved by the last three SolidCraft releases, and the nightly "SolidCraft compatibility" job has failed with this message since 15 November.

It's the number alone that decides: a two-feature box saved by SolidCraft 0.30.1 opens, and the same file with only `"solidcraft/48"` changed to `"solidcraft/58"` is refused.

### What you need and why

SolidCraft releases almost daily and most releases raise the format (48 to 58 between 2 and 17 November). Each step puts FieldCraft behind until the next re-pin (#572, #655, #669, #691), though many of them add things a mesh never touches: a drawing section, a sketch option, plugin data.

### Expected behaviour

Since 0.40.0 SolidCraft opens a newer design with a notice instead of refusing it (tangency-labs/solidcraft#12166). It reads what it knows, keeps a feature it can't read on the timeline as a placeholder that reports an error, and names everything it left out. The commit FieldCraft pins (81dd685) already has that reader (`solidcraft_doc::newer_file`). FieldCraft could use it:

- A newer design in which every feature was read and builds opens as usual, with an entry in `geometry.open`'s `warnings` that names the format and anything left out.
- A newer design with a feature this pin can't read is refused as now, naming the feature. A body built without it could be the wrong shape.
- As far as I can see FieldCraft only reads designs, so the half of that work about keeping unread parts for the next save isn't needed.

The nightly compatibility job would then fail only when a new SolidCraft release changes something FieldCraft reads, which is when a re-pin is really needed.

### Pictures

None.

### References

- #669, whose closing comment describes the current rule (a design from a newer SolidCraft asks for a newer FieldCraft, 2808ed26). The pin then was 0.30.1, which had no reader for newer designs.
- tangency-labs/solidcraft#12166 (the notice and what is kept), and tangency-labs/solidcraft#11319, where I had asked SolidCraft to write older formats instead. This would be the better answer.

title: MCP `open` refuses a SolidCraft `.sc` design by its extension (`geometry.open` opens it)
body:
### Observed failure

The MCP tool `open` refuses a SolidCraft design named `*.sc`:

`open: a .fieldcraft model, a .solidcraft design or a .3mf mesh`

`execute` with `geometry.open` and the same path opens it. `.sc` is what SolidCraft has saved by default for some weeks (tangency-labs/solidcraft#7325: "New designs save as .sc; .solidcraft files still open"), so a design saved by the current app can't be opened with the tool the server's instructions name first.

### Reproduction

1. Save a design as `.sc`, for example with SolidCraft's CLI: `solidcraft-cli run box.json --save box.sc`, where `box.json` is

   ```json
   {"commands": [{"command": "solid.box", "params": {"corner": [0, 0, 0], "length": 20, "width": 20, "height": 20}}]}
   ```
2. `fieldcraft-cli mcp`, then `tools/call` `open {"path": "<folder>/box.sc"}`: the error above.
3. `tools/call` `execute {"command": "geometry.open", "params": {"path": "<folder>/box.sc"}}`: opens, one body.

A copy of the same file named `box.solidcraft` opens with `open`.

### Evidence

Checked with a design saved by SolidCraft 0.30.1 (format 48, a zip container).

### Expected behaviour

`open` takes `.sc` as it takes `.solidcraft`, and its description, error text and the server instructions name both.

### Investigation

`crates/mcp/src/tools.rs`, the `"open"` arm: the extension is matched against `fieldcraft`, `solidcraft` and `3mf` only (develop 52968575).

### Version and platform

FieldCraft develop build of 2026-11-16 (v0.8.0), `fieldcraft-cli mcp`, Windows 11 x86_64; source read at develop 52968575.

title: Solver diagnostics on Windows: the MCP reply's path is `\\?\~\…`, and `crashes list` prints `vv0.8.0`
body:
### Observed failure

Two small display defects in the solver diagnostics of #721. The records themselves are right.

1. **The path in the MCP reply can't be used.** The reply of a failed solve ends with

   `(solver diagnostic: \\?\~\Dev\job\crash\20261118-141738-de741ed967ca8082\report.json)`

   (folder names shortened here). The home folder is replaced by `~` behind the `\\?\` prefix, which isn't a path Windows can open, so a worker reading the reply can't fetch the record from it. `fieldcraft-cli run` prints the plain path (`C:\Users\<me>\Dev\job\crash\…\report.json`) on stderr, and `diagnostics.crash_reports` returns the plain path too.
2. **`fieldcraft-cli crashes list` prints the version with two v's:** `solver_error ×2 in solve.static  vv0.8.0, windows x86_64`.

### Reproduction

Windows, with `FIELDCRAFT_CRASH_DIR` set to a folder under the home folder and inside the write root:

```json
[
  {"command": "file.sample", "params": {"name": "cantilever"}},
  {"command": "model.boundary_condition.edit", "params": {"name": "Clamp", "type": "displacement", "target": {"set": "root"}, "values": [0, null, null, null, null, null]}},
  {"command": "solve.static", "params": {}}
]
```

Send the three commands through `fieldcraft-cli mcp` (`execute`) and read the last reply; then run `fieldcraft-cli crashes list`.

### Evidence

The MCP reply (folder names shortened to `Dev\job`, the rest as received):

```
the stiffness is singular at node 284 in Z: the model can move without straining (missing or insufficient boundary conditions, a part not connected to the rest, or a reference point direction nothing holds) (solver diagnostic: \\?\~\Dev\job\crash\20261118-141738-de741ed967ca8082\report.json)
```

### Expected behaviour

1. A path that can be opened. Either the plain path, as the CLI prints, or, if the home folder should stay out of replies, `~\Dev\job\…` without the `\\?\` prefix.
2. `v0.8.0, windows x86_64`.

One more thing, which may be intended: for this static failure the record's `solve.model.dofs` and `solve.requested_step` are `null`, while `elements` and `nodes` are filled in. For a singular system the number of DOFs is the size one would look for.

### Version and platform

FieldCraft develop build of 2026-11-16 (v0.8.0), `fieldcraft-cli`, Windows 11 x86_64.

title: Add an optional NGSolve backend for user-defined PDEs and magnetic forces
body:
### Current behaviour

FieldCraft can prepare tagged meshes and run its built-in analyses. I couldn't find a documented way to run a user-defined finite-element formulation on a FieldCraft model or bring the resulting fields and integral quantities back into the workflow.

### What you need and why

I'd like to use FieldCraft to set up geometry and mesh regions, then solve my own field equations with NGSolve. My first use case is finding the force and torque on a steel armature driven by a current-fed coil or a permanent magnet, for example to plot force versus air gap. I'd also like to model time-dependent or frequency-domain magnetodynamics when eddy currents matter.

The same integration could support other scalar, vector, or mixed PDEs through user-defined weak forms. The broader electromagnetic and particle-beam use case is discussed in #660.

### Expected behaviour

- Expose a tagged volume mesh with consistent units and named volume and boundary groups. For a magnetic setup, these can identify the air domain, coil, magnet, steel and outer boundary.
- Let me run a user-selected Python script with a separately installed Netgen/NGSolve as an optional external solver. The script defines the finite-element spaces, weak forms, sources, material laws and post-processing. A reproducible CLI workflow would be a useful first step.
- Return scalar and vector fields in VTU and named integral results such as force and torque in a machine-readable format. It would be useful to pass those resultants to a FieldCraft structural step as loads.
- Include a runnable 3D magnetostatic example with an air gap, using a permanent magnet or a DC coil. Compute the magnetic flux density and total force with the Maxwell stress tensor on a closed surface in air, and show that the force converges under mesh refinement. A transient or harmonic coil example with eddy currents could follow.

### References

- [NGSolve's 3D permanent-magnet tutorial](https://docu.ngsolve.org/latest/i-tutorials/unit-2.4-Maxwell/Maxwell.html)
- [NGSolve's coil magnetostatics tutorial](https://ngsolve.org/ngsolve/docs/i-tutorials/wta/coil.html)
- [FieldCraft's documented mesh and geometry tags](https://tangency-labs.github.io/fieldcraft/formats/fieldcraft.html#meshbin)

### Working demo

My [FieldCraft fork release](https://github.com/JohannesMaierhofer/fieldcraft/releases/tag/ngsolve-v0.8.1-r2) and [Python bridge](https://github.com/JohannesMaierhofer/fieldcraft-ngsolve/tree/74393901cf1b6fe70e5956003f948c9fe5eee889) run a user-selected NGSolve script on a named FieldCraft mesh and show the returned fields and integrals on that mesh. The [magnetic diffusion example](https://github.com/JohannesMaierhofer/fieldcraft-ngsolve/tree/74393901cf1b6fe70e5956003f948c9fe5eee889/examples/magnetic-diffusion) replays 17 snapshots on a common colour scale in the desktop app.

The [3D armature example](https://github.com/JohannesMaierhofer/fieldcraft-ngsolve/tree/74393901cf1b6fe70e5956003f948c9fe5eee889/examples/armature) now uses magnetic virtual work at fixed excitation for force and torque. It reports all three components about the armature centre and about an offset point. At a 4 mm air gap, the finest mesh (294,912 tetrahedra) gives an axial force of −3.09053 mN and a side-point torque about z of −6.17918 µN·m. From the previous refinement the axial force changes by 0.433% and the side-point torque vector by 0.447%. The study covers three gaps and four mesh resolutions. Independently displaced and rotated field solves check the sign. The report retains the Maxwell-stress comparison and distinguishes mesh convergence from uncertainty in material data and outer boundary placement.

title: lbm: the TRT bulk collision grows below τ⁺ ≈ 0.5025 at Ma 0.087 with Λ = 3/16
body:
The D3Q19 TRT bulk collision is linearly unstable just above τ⁺ = 1/2 at moderate Mach number, with the default magic parameter Λ = 3/16.

**Evidence** (#832, heavy test `crates/lbm/tests/trt_stability.rs`): a von Neumann linearisation about ρ = 1, u = (0.05, 0, 0) (Ma 0.087), following Sterling & Chen 1996 (Eq. 31–33) and Wissocq, Sagaut & Boussuge 2019 (App. B.2). It takes the largest growth over all modes of a 16³ periodic box, with no boundaries.

| τ⁺ | Λ | U | largest growth per step |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5005 | 3/16 | 0.05 | 1.96e-3 (grows) |
| 0.501 | 3/16 | 0.05 | 8.9e-4 |
| 0.502 | 3/16 | 0.05 | 7.5e-6 |
| ≥ 0.5025 | 3/16 | 0.05 | neutral |
| 0.5005 | 3/16 | 0.01 | neutral |
| 0.5005 | ≤ 3e-5 | 0.05 | neutral (16³, 32³ and 64³) |

The nonlinear periodic box confirms each row. The growing modes are oblique.

**Scope:** #832's velocity inlet is accepted with τ⁺ ≥ 0.505 as its criterion, and setup warns below 0.505. Running below that (high Reynolds number on coarse grids) needs the bulk collision itself to be stable there.

**Ask:** from the literature, find how to make the bulk stable for 0.5 < τ⁺ < 0.505 at Mach ≲ 0.1. Possible routes include a different Λ, or regularised or recursive-regularised collision (RR/HRR are already in the solver). Measure each route against the linear analysis above and against published benchmarks. Constants come from theory or a cited source (AGENTS.md), never from tuning.

title: Help wanted: run-to-run and cross-machine reproducibility of a channel case (same input, same commit)
body:
We need to know how much Fieldcraft channel results change when nothing in the input changes. Then code changes can be judged against the real scatter rather than against noise.

Please run the P1 input from #937 with `"collision": "mrt"`; that case completes 4,000 steps. Use unpatched `11ca41a6b3a43d18e61d1b906c77f547ea5f7e4d`, and also current develop.

## Matrix (change one factor at a time)

1. Same binary, same machine, run twice: are the outputs bitwise identical?
2. Same binary with `threads` = 1, 2, 4 and 8.
3. A rebuilt binary on a different machine, OS or CPU (and compiler version), at the same commit.
4. The GPU backend against the CPU, if you have one.

## Please report for each run

- The commit, `rustc --version`, the build command and the binary's SHA256.
- The OS and CPU (or the GPU and driver) and the thread count.
- The exit code and the SHA256 of each output frame.
- The final maximum Mach, the final mean streamwise velocity, and the relative change in mass.

If outputs differ, the first step or frame where they diverge is the most useful detail.

For statistics over a longer window, the wall-modelled channel inputs from #938 can be used with the same matrix. For those, please report the mean friction (u_τ) and the averaging window for each run, and post every run, including failed ones.

Related: #937, #938.

title: Help wanted: refinement order of curved-wall drag for a periodic sphere array in Stokes flow (analytic reference)
Help wanted: external-flow drag benchmarks (sphere Re 100, Schäfer–Turek cylinder 2D-2, cylinder Re 3900)
Help wanted: wall-modelled channel LES vs Lee & Moser DNS at Re_tau ≈ 950 and 2000
Help wanted: TRT with `musker` and a porous trip fails at step 2,887 in a periodic channel; MRT completes 4,000 (reproducer included)
body:
On unpatched commit `11ca41a6b3a43d18e61d1b906c77f547ea5f7e4d`, the command script below fails with TRT at step 2,887, reporting a lattice speed of 0.501 against the solver's 0.5 limit. Changing only `collision` to `mrt` completes all 4,000 steps.

P2 raises the initial x velocity to 22.420131035185296 and shows the same contrast: TRT fails at step 2,629 (lattice speed 0.502), and MRT completes.

Each case was reproduced through both `fieldcraft-cli run` and an MCP `batch`. The MCP process exits 0 even when the solve fails; its tool result has `isError: true` and names the same step.

## Reproduce

Build with `cargo build --release -p fieldcraft-cli -j 2 --locked` (Rust 1.99.1, Linux x86_64; binary SHA256 `177cf3df189b594a5b8a6e8c6584a094955a9c7a4d4e037a10e2848e8211ad8d`). Save the script as `p1-trt.json` and run `fieldcraft-cli run p1-trt.json`:

```json
[
 {"command": "model.units", "params": {"system": "m-kg-s-N-Pa"}},
 {"command": "model.material.create", "params": {"name": "Fluid", "density": 1.0, "fluid": {"type": "newtonian", "viscosity": 0.0010526315789473684}}},
 {"command": "model.fluid_domain.create", "params": {"name": "Channel", "material": "Fluid", "min": [0, 0, 0], "max": [6.3, 2, 6.3], "spacing": 0.1, "faces": {"x_min": {"type": "periodic"}, "x_max": {"type": "periodic"}, "z_min": {"type": "periodic"}, "z_max": {"type": "periodic"}}, "initial_velocity": [19.49576611755243, 0, 0], "acceleration": [1, 0, 0], "porous": [{"name": "Trip", "min": [2.6, 0.3, 2.6], "max": [3.6, 1.1, 3.6], "axis": "x", "resistance": {"type": "loss_coefficient", "coefficient": 0.2}}]}},
 {"command": "model.step.create", "params": {"name": "Run", "procedure": {"type": "fluid", "domain": "Channel", "steps": 4000, "time_step": 0.0005129318817072185, "frames": 8, "collision": "trt", "turbulence": {"type": "smagorinsky", "constant": 0.08, "wall_model": "musker"}}}},
 {"command": "solve.fluid", "params": {"step": "Run", "backend": "cpu", "threads": 2}}
]
```

## Setup

- 63 × 20 × 63 cells; τ = 0.5001619784889602; TRT magic parameter 0.1875 (the default).
- Viscosity and forcing come from a nominal Re_τ = 950.
- The untripped control, started from a uniform flow, completes 4,000 steps with both TRT and MRT.
- MRT completing is not a validated turbulence result: its largest saved-frame Mach number is 0.288 (P1) and 0.317 (P2).

Fresh shorter runs (only `steps` changed) give the final maximum Mach for P1 / P2:

| steps | P1 | P2 |
|---|---|---|
| 500 | 0.1828 | 0.2108 |
| 1000 | 0.1872 | 0.2189 |
| 1500 | 0.1970 | 0.2234 |
| 2000 | 0.2109 | 0.2394 |
| 2500 | 0.3280 | 0.4341 |
| 2600 | — | 0.5097 |
| 2800 | 0.4407 | — |

The existing warning already flags τ close to ½ and recommends `regularized`, so no new warning is proposed.

## How you can help

Each run takes about 2 minutes on 2 threads. Please post the commit, OS/CPU, the CLI exit code, and either the failing step or "completes 4000", for any of:

1. P1/P2 on your machine, and on current develop.
2. One-factor ablations of P1, changing exactly one thing:
   - remove the porous block;
   - turn the wall model off;
   - set the collision to `regularized`;
   - set the TRT magic parameter to 1/4 or 1/12;
   - move τ further from ½ (smaller `time_step`, same physical viscosity).
3. The GPU backend, if you have one.

These would show which of the porous forcing, the wall model, the low τ or the TRT collision drives the growth.

Related: #785, #790.
